title: Does every biometric collection point have documented consent and tested accuracy safeguards?
description: A board-level oversight question testing whether an organisation's biometric systems have both a documented legal basis for collection and independently confirmed accuracy before any biometric match affects a real person.
question_text: For every point in our systems where biometric data (facial images, fingerprints, voiceprints) is collected or matched, do we have a documented legal basis and consent record, and — separately — has the accuracy of any matching system been independently tested across demographic groups, with a human required to confirm any match before it triggers action against a real person?
rationale: Rite Aid and Clearview AI represent the two most common ways biometric governance fails: acting on unconfirmed, biased matches (Rite Aid), and collecting biometric data without consent in the first place (Clearview). Both led to major regulatory enforcement.
follow_up_actions: Request the current biometric consent record and facial-recognition accuracy/human-review log.
Confirm no biometric match automatically triggers an adverse action without independent human confirmation.
Ask whether any biometric data source (including third-party or scraped data) lacks documented consent.

citations.title: Rite Aid Banned from Using AI Facial Recognition After FTC Says Retailer Deployed Technology without Reasonable Safeguards
